balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For Kingsoft Corporation Limited: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For Kingsoft Corporation Limited: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

ebitda.title: EBITDA
ebitda.content:
EBITDA is earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation -- an operating-cash proxy that ignores capital intensity.

For Kingsoft Corporation Limited: read it beside CapEx: a business that must reinvest most of its EBITDA is not as cash-generative as the margin suggests.

What to watch:

  • EBITDA margin trend
  • Gap between EBITDA and operating cash flow (working capital)

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For Kingsoft Corporation Limited: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For Kingsoft Corporation Limited: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

segmentRevenue.title: Segment revenue: Office vs Games vs Cloud
segmentRevenue.content:
Kingsoft reports two live segments: Office software (WPS -- subscriptions, advertising and institutional licensing) and Online games (principally JX Online III and its mobile spin-offs, plus new titles). Cloud was a third segment reported only in FY2018-FY2019, before Kingsoft Cloud was deconsolidated and separately listed.

For Kingsoft Corporation Limited: Office overtook Games as the larger segment and grew to roughly 61% of FY2025 revenue while Games declined that year; new game titles launched from January 2026 are the catalyst being watched for a Games recovery.

What to watch:

  • Office's growth rate versus Games' trajectory -- is the mix shift still widening?
  • Whether new game launches arrest the Games segment's decline
  • Cloud only has two data points and predates deconsolidation -- not a current driver

nciProfit.title: Net income vs profit attributable to non-controlling interests
nciProfit.content:
Net income is Kingsoft's consolidated profit, including the portion earned by minority shareholders of subsidiaries. Profit attributable to NCI is specifically the share of that profit owned by outside minority shareholders of Kingsoft Office Software (listed separately in China), not by 3888.HK's own shareholders.

For Kingsoft Corporation Limited: NCI profit has grown fast as Kingsoft Office's earnings have grown -- from RMB870.7m in FY2025 to RMB1,516.2m in H1 FY2026 alone -- so a rising share of consolidated net income is not available to 3888.HK shareholders. The DCF's owner FCF and per-share metrics should be read net of this.

What to watch:

  • NCI profit growing faster than consolidated net income (dilution of the parent's economic share)
  • Kingsoft Office's own ownership stake and any changes to it

subscribers.title: WPS paying subscribers: total vs overseas
subscribers.content:
Subscribers is WPS's total paying-subscriber count; overseas subscribers is the subset outside mainland China, only disclosed from FY2024.

For Kingsoft Corporation Limited: overseas subscribers grew from 1.74m to 2.85m (+64%) in one year, far faster than the total base -- management's qualitative emphasis is that international expansion is the next leg of WPS subscription growth as the domestic base matures.

What to watch:

  • Overseas subscriber growth rate relative to total subscriber growth
  • Overseas as a rising share of the total (only two years of data so far)

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For Kingsoft Corporation Limited: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For Kingsoft Corporation Limited: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For Kingsoft Corporation Limited: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For Kingsoft Corporation Limited: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For Kingsoft Corporation Limited: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
